key_insight: Reframing 4-bit AdamW quantization in preconditioner space, rather than state space, better preserves the second-moment behavior that drives adaptive updates.
engineering_relevance: This improves low-memory training for large language models by reducing optimizer-state storage while narrowing the validation-loss gap to full 32-bit AdamW.
method: ZIP-SR: keep zero in the second-moment codebook and use stochastic rounding probabilities in preconditioner space.
ZE-EDEN: use a zero-excluding second-moment codebook with calibration to counter the positive quantization floor.
Use 4-bit NF4 for the first moment and targeted stochastic rounding of the LM-head first moment during the final 10% of training.
evidence_signal: Across GPT- and Llama-style pretraining from 130M to 2.7B parameters, both methods reduced TorchAO 4-bit AdamW's mean validation-loss gap to 32-bit AdamW at every evaluated scale, with up to 70% reduction, and also improved supervised fine-tuning results.
watch_item: These gains depend on careful codebook design and calibration, so implementation details of the second-moment quantizer may strongly affect stability and reproducibility.
paper_title: Rounding in Preconditioner Space: Redesigning 4-bit AdamW Optimizer-State Quantization
